plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: Fields of velvety, silvery-green leaves rise into spikes of fragrant, pea-like blossoms. Each spike is deep blue, tipped with a crisp white crown that ages to magenta. Whole roadsides and meadows turn to rippling blue.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to May, with peak color typically from late March through April
plants.location: Texas, USA, especially the Hill Country and central Texas prairies
plants.funFact: The white tips on bluebonnet flowers turn reddish-purple after pollination. This signals to bees that the flower has already been visited, so they move on to unpollinated ones.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: Leafless stems shoot up from bare ground, each carrying a cluster of sweetly scented, trumpet-shaped pink blooms. The flowers open as the leaves have died back, so they appear to float in the late-summer landscape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer, February to March in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southwestern Cape of South Africa, including the Western Cape coastal and mountain slopes
plants.funFact: It is nicknamed the 'naked lady' because the flower stalks appear with no leaves at all. The foliage grows in the cooler, wetter months and dies back before the flowers emerge.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A towering Himalayan tree that bursts into huge, goblet-shaped blooms on bare branches, in shades from pale blush to vivid rose-pink. In full flower, the whole crown looks like a cloud of pink against the mountains.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, March to May
plants.location: Eastern Himalaya, including Bhutan, Nepal, Sikkim and southwest China, as well as gardens in mild climates
plants.funFact: Seedlings of this magnolia can take around 25 years or more to flower for the first time, which is why gardeners prize named, grafted selections.
